full_judgment:
2. All these four appeals are taken up together for hearing and disposed of by this common judgment as all of them have arisen out of the same judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 6-5-2002 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong in Special Case No. 151 of 1999 arising out of Bandar Police Station Case No. 7(12)87 dated 8-12-87 corresponding to DAB GR No. 42 of 1987 convicting the accused- appellants under sections 409/420/467/468/471/477(A)/201/109 of the Penal Code and 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 15 years and to pay a fine of Taka 14,00,000 only each in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 years. 

 3. The prosecution case, in short, as it appears from the first information report is that Abu Md Arif Siddique, Inspector DAB, Chittagong lodged the first information report with Bandar Police Station Chittagong on 8-12-1987 alleging, inter alia that the accused-appellant namely. Abul Khair, while posted as Manager, Pubali Bank Limited. North Patenga Branch, Chittagong illegally started business with his younger brother accused Abul Hossain and another accused namely SM Rafique in the name and style Tenico Industries Limited and illegally opened a CC Account No.2 in the name of aforesaid Tenico Industries Limited Later on, accused-appellant Abul Khair with the help of other accused persons misappropriated Taka 10,00,000 vide cheque No. 050672 dated 2-7-1985, Taka 10,00,000 vide cheque No. 050673 dated 2-7-1985, Taka 10,00,000 vide cheque No. 050674 and Taka 85,000 vide cheque No. 050658 dated 25-8-1985 without entering the same in the ledger book and misappropriated an amount of Taka 30,85,000 only. It is also alleged that the aforesaid cheques were not posted in the ledger book but it is mentioned in the payment register, scroll register and daily accounts register. Moreover, the accused bank Officers and other accused persons also misappropriated Taka 44,00,000 on 1-1-86, Taka 3,00,000 on 6-3-86, Taka 4,00,000 on 9-3-86 and Taka 11,00,000 on 23-7-86 in total Taka 62,00,000 without entering the same in the ledger book. But it appears that the amount is only shown in the payment register, scroll book and daily account register. It is further alleged that the accused bank manager namely, Abul Khair with the help of other accuseds namely, Abul Hossain, SM Rafique, the proprietor of Messrs Tenico Industries Ltd, SM Golam Khaleque, Ex Cashier, Abdul Awal Ex-Officer, Kamal-ul-Alam and Sharifullah, Ex Officer of Pubali Bank Ltd, North Patenga Branch, Chittagong misappropriated in Total Taka 92,85,000 by misusing their official capacity and by commission of the criminal breach of trust and forgery during the period from 1-1-86 to 23-7-86 and, as such, first information report was lodged by the informant against those accused persons. 

 4. The investigation of the case was entrusted to Abu Md Arif Siddique, Inspector, DAB Chittagong who visited the place of occurrence, seized alamats of the case and recorded the evidence of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and subsequently, Inspector Jatindra Nath Podder, DAB Chittagong submitted Memo of Evidence for sanction after completion of the investigation and after getting sanction Md Islam, Anti-Corruption Officer, Chittagong submitted charge-sheet being No. 47 dated 23-3-95 under sections 409/420/467/468/471/477(A)/201/109 of the Penal Code and also under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the accused-appellants. 

 5. The case record was ultimately transferred to the Court of the learned Senior Special Judge, Chittagong on 31-3-96 who took cognisance of the case against the accused persons under sections 409/420/467/468/471/477(A)/201/109 of the Penal Code and also under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sent the case record for trial on 17-6-99. 

 8. Prosecution examined 8 witnesses to substantiate the case against the accused persons including the accused appellants. After completion of the trial the learned Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong by impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 6-5-2002 in Special Case No. 151 of 1999 convicted the accused appellants as aforesaid. 

 9. In Criminal Appeal No. 4210 of 2003 Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Counsel appeared on behalf of the accused-appellant Abul Khair. He along with other Counsels representing Criminal Appeal Nos. 1825, 1891 and 1751 of 2002 without making elaborate submissions contending different points, mainly submitted that all these cases hinge only on the point, whether the said cases come within the mischief of proviso to section 222(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 If the law is explained we find that an allegation of criminal breach of trust involving dishonest misappropriation of money in respect of which the offence is committed on different dates, the time included the first and last day shall not exceed one year. In the present case the total amount defalcated i.e. Taka 92,85,000 on different dates starting from 25-3-85 to 23-7-86 is found to have clearly exceeded one year, as such, the charge is totally a defective one which is clearly made in violation of proviso to section 222(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 11. In many decisions it has been held that this defect of charge when it comes within the mischief of proviso of section 222(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not curable under section 537 of the Code. This proposition of law has been decided in various decisions of the Courts of this sub- continent. In the case of Md Mosaddar Haque and another vs State reported in 10 DLR (SC) 29 where it was held: "No question as to whether prejudice was caused or not need be considered as illegality" has resulted from adopting a mode of trial prohibited by the Code and it cannot, therefore, be cured under section 537 CrPC. 

 12. Reflection of this decision can also be found in the case of Md Abdul Bari Molla vs State reported in 1997 BLD 223 = 3 BLC 474 where the said provision of law was applied and held that the trial was held by adopting a mode which is prohibited by law and, as such, the same is illegal not curable under section 537, CrPC Similarly, Mansur Ali vs State 39 DLR 184. Sk Abdul Majid vs State 1987 BLD 413 = 39 DLR 414. Alfazuddin vs State 45 DLR 352. Abul Kalam Azad vs State 48 DLR (AD) 294. ASM Faruq vs State 22 DLR 539. AIR 1986 (PC) 53. Shid Nath Westhi vs Emperor 33 CWN 454. AIR 1943 (Lahore) 304. AIR 1945 (Bombay) 413 echoed on the same point. 

 13. In this case we have seen that Taka 85,000 was defalcated on 25-3-85, Taka 30,00,000 was defalcated on 2-7-85 by three cheques on the same day, Taka 44,000 on 1-1-86, Taka 3,00,000, Taka 4,00,000 on 9-3-86 and lastly, Taka 11,00,000 on 23-7-86 which clearly shows that from the first date to last date i.e. 25-3-85 to 23-7-86 in which the total amount of Taka 92,85,000 was defalcated clearly exceeded one year and, as such, attracted the provision of section 222(2) proviso of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 15. Accordingly, all these four appeals are allowed. The impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence are set aside. The case is sent back on remand to the trial Court to hold a fresh trial in accordance with law and accordingly, the trial Court is directed to conclude the trial as early as possible preferably within a period of 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order by the trial Court.
